lines.trans: Hello, dear guests, welcome to our restaurant!
Hello, and where is your mustache?
I shaved it off this morning.
Without a mustache I simply look younger.
Indeed, it suits you much better this way.
Lenochka said that you would treat us to lunch.

Please have a seat at this table.

examples.text: Ведь это же был ваш личный телефон!
examples.trans: After all, that was your personal phone!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'at least', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я хотела поговорить с тобой насчёт Кати.
examples.trans: I wanted to talk to you about Katya.

examples.text: Катя, мы с девочками хотели вечером посидеть.
examples.trans: Katya, the girls and I wanted to hang out tonight.

examples.text: Вообще-то мы хотели спокойно посидеть девочками.
examples.trans: Actually we wanted to sit quietly with the girls.

meanings.en: to warn, to give advance notice
meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'упреждать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to warn', paired with 'предупредить'.

examples.text: Шеф, вы бы меня хоть предупреждали!
examples.trans: Chef, you could at least warn me!

examples.text: Я тебя предупреждал.
examples.trans: I warned you.

examples.text: Предупреждаю тебя последний раз.
examples.trans: I am warning you for the last time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'yourself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он высокий и с красивыми усами.
examples.trans: He is tall and has a handsome mustache.

examples.text: Может, самое время Денису подойти к ней?
examples.trans: Maybe this is the right time for Denis to approach her?

examples.text: Пусть они лучше сами во всём разбираются.
examples.trans: Let them figure everything out by themselves.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты что, только не этот Денис!
examples.trans: What are you talking about, anyone but Denis!

examples.text: Сегодня вечером будем только мы вдвоём.
examples.trans: Tonight it will be just the two of us.

examples.text: Костя, только много мне не наливай.
examples.trans: Kostya, just do not pour me too much.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Любимый мужчина готовит мне вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: My beloved man is cooking me a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Тем более я гениальный шеф-повар.
examples.trans: Especially since I am a brilliant head chef.

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to recognise; to find out', paired with 'узнавать'.

examples.text: Лёва, я сам только что об этом узнал.
examples.trans: Lyova, I only just found out about it myself.

examples.text: Ты меня узнал?
examples.trans: Did you recognise me?

examples.text: Я узнаю, где он.
examples.trans: I'll find out where he is.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Просто Лёва немного робкий и хороший.
examples.trans: Lyova is simply a bit shy and kind.

examples.text: Хорошо тебя дома родители воспитали.
examples.trans: Your parents raised you well at home.

examples.text: Ну хорошо, давай попробуем это сделать.
examples.trans: Well alright, let us try to do that.

meanings.en: to make it, to be in time
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'managed', paired with 'успевать'.

examples.text: Важно успеть сделать в жизни побольше.
examples.trans: It is important to manage to do more in life.

examples.text: Хорошо, что я успел сориентироваться.
examples.trans: It is a good thing I managed to think fast.

examples.text: Я не успел позвонить.
examples.trans: I didn't manage to call.

сориентироваться.gloss: to think fast / get one's bearings

meanings.en: to think fast / get one's bearings
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ориентироваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think fast / get one's bearings'.

related.gloss: not to to think fast (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Хорошо, что я успел сориентироваться.
examples.trans: It is a good thing I managed to think fast.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и сориентироваться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to think fast on time.
